html:
SMTO-SKL-0012 — Choose which Google account to use for Calendar

GUID: 92886db3-7036-5b43-9d2b-e1116e520e96
Slug: google-calendar-account-ambiguous
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • More than one of your connected Google accounts can use Google Calendar, and SMTO won't guess which one you meant. Nothing was sent to Google.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you're not sure which accounts are connected, ask SMTO to list your connected Google accounts. The list shows each account's email address and what Calendar access it has.
  2. Ask for the calendar task again and say which account to use, for example by giving that account's email address. With one account named, SMTO knows exactly whose calendar to read or change.
  3. If the task should always use one account, mention that account each time you ask about your calendar in this conversation. SMTO never picks an account on its own, so it asks whenever more than one could fit.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the calendar task and the result names the account you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete a connected Google account from Parameter Store just to avoid choosing; you'd have to connect it again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google account resolution found more than one eligible google_account for the Calendar operation and no explicit account_ref or single accepted account binding, so it refused to choose.

What this means

  • Shared account resolution finds multiple eligible Google accounts and no unique accepted or explicit account selection. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Shared account resolution finds multiple eligible Google accounts and no unique accepted or explicit account selection.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect safe account candidates and the task's accepted account identity.

How to fix it

  • Read the candidate accounts in the error details or from google_calendar.accounts, then pass the intended exact account_ref on the Calendar tool call (or bind one account in the conversation). Do not select an account by storage order.
  • Inspect google_calendar.accounts and pass the intended exact account_ref. Do not select by storage order.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect google_calendar.accounts and pass the intended exact account_ref. Do not select by storage order.

How to verify the fix

  • The request names the intended exact account_ref.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
